response.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT c.district_id, di.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS client_count FROM client c JOIN district di ON di.district_id = c.district_id GROUP BY c.district_id, di.A3) SELECT district_id, region, client_count, client_count * 1.0 / SUM(client_count) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS share_of_region, client_count * 1.0 / SUM(client_count) OVER () AS share_of_total FROM d ORDER BY share_of_total DESC, district_id LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Region and overall totals are sums of clients counted by client.district_id (every client has a matching district via the foreign key). Districts with no clients are not listed.
Ties at the 10th place are broken by district_id ascending, so exactly 10 rows are returned.
Shares are returned as unrounded decimal fractions (not percentages).
